thesis: Open position from 2026-08-18 at 27.60, now 27.64 — flat, and the thesis is a multi-year re-rating rather than a move. The mispricing is visible in two fetched numbers that disagree with each other: only 38.9% of covering analysts are bullish and that share is still falling, while the company has beaten consensus in each of the last three reported quarters by 11.37%, 3.55% and 14.29%. A business that consistently beats while its analyst base gets more negative is one where the published estimates, not the business, are what is wrong. Downside case is 23.50, or about 8.1x, which is where this is worth owning even if the pipeline disappoints.
key_risk: The concrete invalidation, since there is deliberately no stop: two consecutive quarters of EPS misses against consensus, or guidance that puts post-LOE revenue replacement materially behind schedule, would mean the beats were cost-driven rather than a real earnings base and the 14.5x multiple is not owed. counter_argument: The strongest case against is that 38.9% bullish and deteriorating is not necessarily a contrarian signal — it may simply be correct, and the consistent beats may be cost cuts and buybacks against a shrinking revenue base rather than evidence of an earnings floor. I cannot fully answer that from what was fetched today: I have three quarters of EPS actuals but no revenue trajectory, so the quality of the beats is asserted rather than demonstrated. The multiple, not the growth, has to carry the idea.

This is the position best supported by what the Fed actually did on 2026-09-16: it hiked to 3.75-4.00%, projects core PCE at 3.4% for 2026, and its own median dot implies another hike to 4.1% before year-end with no cut until 2028. Chair Warsh said inflation is too high and has been for too long. A central bank still tightening against 3.4% core inflation is the plainest case there is for long-duration Treasuries continuing lower, and a 20-year-plus ETF is the purest short expression available on this venue.
key_risk: Short duration is the crowded side of this trade and the squeeze risk is real — TLT rallied 1.11% on 2026-09-17, the day after the hike, against the position. The 83.30 stop is only 1.75% above the entry, so a single risk-off session closes it. If inflation rolls over faster than the SEP assumes, or if growth cracks and the market prices cuts through 2027 against the dots, long bonds rally hard. Being short requires margin and the position can gap beyond the stop.
counter_argument: The strongest case against is that most of the move has already happened: TLT is only 1.64% above its 120-day low of 80.46, so the obvious chart target is roughly where price already sits, and reaching 78.00 requires breaking to new lows rather than continuing to one. The sharper version is that the hike is already in the price — the market knew it was coming and bonds *rose* the next session anyway, which is exactly the behaviour of an asset that has finished discounting the news. If the long end does not extend past roughly 5.3%, this position does not pay from here even if the direction is right.

thesis: Open position from 2026-08-21 at 65.60, now 66.91 (+2.0%). The honest statement today is that this position is working for reasons other than the one it was bought for: EEM is outperforming, up 2.40% over a month against SPY at -0.63%, and it rose 1.81% on 2026-09-17. What it is NOT is a Fed-easing trade — the Committee hiked on 2026-09-16 — so the position rests on measured relative strength and its own levels, not on a policy tailwind.
key_risk: The macro is now pointing the wrong way and that is the main risk. A Fed hiking to 3.75-4.00% with another hike in its own dots supports the dollar, and a firmer dollar is the most reliable historical headwind for emerging-market equity. EM debt is financed in dollars, so tightening US policy plus a 5.01% 10-year tightens global financial conditions directly. This position is held, not added to, for exactly that reason.
counter_argument: The strongest case against is now the macro itself, and it is not answered: the original thesis for this position was a Fed easing cycle, that thesis has been checked against the primary source and is false, and an idea whose stated driver turns out not to exist deserves scepticism even when the price is cooperating. EEM is also still -5.33pp behind SPY over three months and -2.41% outright, so the one-month leadership is a recent turn rather than an established trend, and the 71.50 target sits within 0.1% of the 120-day high of 71.57 — this needs a breakout to a new range high to pay.

thesis: Open position from 2026-08-22 at 398.00, now 398.36 — flat after four weeks, and reported as flat. The one leg of the case that survives checking the Fed statement is the inflation leg: the Committees own projections carry 3.7% PCE and 3.4% core PCE for 2026, which is what gold is a claim on. The easing leg does not survive — the Fed hiked to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16.
key_risk: Conviction 2 and the thinness is the point: the single confirmation behind it is technical. Worse, the macro has been checked and is hostile — a hiking Fed raises both nominal and real short rates, and the opportunity cost of holding a non-yielding asset against a 5.01% 10-year rises every day the position stays open. GLD has underperformed SPY by 25.73pp over six months. Sized at 1% and should not be added to.
counter_argument: The strongest case against is that gold is being asked to work against its two most reliable headwinds at once — rising real rates and a firming dollar — on the strength of an inflation print the Fed is actively and successfully tightening against. The SEP has core PCE falling to 2.5% by 2027, so even the surviving leg of the thesis is projected to fade. The position is flat after a month, is 11.2% below its own 120-day high and is measurably not leading anything. A reasonable reader could close this rather than hold it; it is kept only because it is sized at 1%.
